Inventory Write-off — Edit

The Inventory Write — Off form allows you to record the removal of inventory items from your stock when they are lost, damaged, stolen, expired, or otherwise cannot be sold.

When you create an inventory write-off, the system automatically reduces the quantity on hand for the selected items and records the appropriate expense in your accounts.

Common reasons for inventory write-offs include product damage during storage, theft, expiration of perishable goods, obsolescence, or inventory count discrepancies.

The following fields are available on this form:

Date

Enter the date of the inventory write-off. This determines when the inventory adjustment and expense are recorded.

The write-off date affects inventory valuation and when the loss appears in your profit and loss statement.

Reference

Enter a reference number for this write-off. This could be an adjustment number or incident report reference.

References help track inventory losses and link to supporting documentation like damage reports or disposal certificates.

Inventory Location

Select the inventory location from which items are being written off. Leave blank to write off from unspecified location.

If you track inventory by location, select where the loss occurred. Otherwise, leave blank for general inventory.

Description

Optionally, add a description explaining the reason for the write-off, such as 'Water damage' or 'Expired products'.

Good descriptions provide an audit trail and help identify patterns in inventory losses for better control.

Items

Enter the inventory items to write off. Each line represents a different item and quantity to remove from stock.

The system will reduce inventory quantities and record the cost as an expense or capitalize it to an asset.

Allocation

Select the account to allocate the write-off expense. This is typically an expense account like 'Inventory write-offs'.

You can also select a fixed asset account if the inventory is being used to construct or improve an asset.

Fixed Asset

If allocating to a fixed asset account, select the specific fixed asset to capitalize the inventory cost.

This is used when inventory items are consumed in building or improving a fixed asset rather than being lost.

Tax Code

Select a tax code if the write-off has tax implications, such as GST/VAT adjustments.

Tax codes ensure proper VAT/GST treatment when inventory with claimable input tax is written off.

Project

Optionally assign this write-off to a specific project for project cost tracking.

Project allocation helps track inventory losses by project and affects project profitability reports.

Division

Optionally assign this write-off to a specific division for divisional reporting.

Division allocation helps analyze inventory losses by business segment or location.
